A modern airspace needs the right radars. RTX is ramping up their production.
items.summary: The U.S. airspace is congested, complex – and, for right now, relying on radars that were never built for that volume or variety of aircraft. To manage that mix of commercial flights, manned military aircraft, UAVs and even space launches, operators need real-time, pinpoint-accurate data showing where aircraft are and how they relate to one another. Fast facts 45,000 flights a day (in U.S. airspace) Traffic expected to double by 2040 Collins Aerospace, an RTX business, was selected by the Federal Aviation Administration to help accelerate that effort with two radars that are now central to the modernization push: The Condor Mk3, and the ASR-XM. Both are made at Collins’ site in Largo, Florida, which is undergoing a $26.5 capacity-expansion project. Here’s how those radars – and scaling up their production – will make the modern airspace more manageable.
